proofStatus: All entry fixtures and capability proof records are planned; none was executed by CE-00.1.
policy: Every one of the 1,108 research-inventory entries has exactly one disposition, one owner lot, one capability family and a proof-fixture requirement. No entry leaves the denominator.
Counts are tracking denominators. No support percentage is derived from type occurrence, registry or profile counts.
A required entry is stable in-profile work until its proof record closes with the listed evidence classes. Upstream emission observations are comparator evidence (E1), not PandamStyle qualification.
Runtime-unbounded needs and unsupported platforms stay visible as limitations.

Entry fields sources, bcd, bcdRelations, alpha1, upstream are recorded upstream facts; every other field and section is derived from them and the authored inputs by tests/core-evolution/tools/derive-registry.mjs, and the validator re-derives and compares the whole registry.

canonical-property.definition: A standard-track CSS property recognized by the PandamStyle descriptor catalog. Recognition never grants consumer access to arbitrary values.
canonical-property.proof: Required entries: accepted finite domains and structured rejections (E2), emitted and transformed CSS (E3) and computed behavior in each profile target (E4). Recognized but not required entries: either the same proof when admitted, or a structured diagnostic fixture (E2).

normalized-alias.definition: Another spelling of exactly one canonical property or scoped platform extension with the same grammar: a BCD prefix/alternative name whose statements carry no grammar caveat, a legacy name alias or an upstream shorthand key. Behavior caveats from BCD are recorded with an alias audit. The canonical property carries the requirement.
normalized-alias.proof: Normalization or a diagnostic naming the canonical property (E2), and emitted CSS equivalent to the canonical form (E3). CE-02 decides whether the spelling is accepted or diagnosed; prefix emission belongs to the CE-01 transformation.

system-resource.definition: Expressed through a design-system-owned resource (typed custom property, font-face descriptor, gradient, mask, shadow, filter or transform composition, focus treatment or declaration bundle) rather than a free property value.
system-resource.proof: Resource definition admission and reference resolution (E2) and emitted CSS (E3); computed behavior (E4) through the carrying capability's proof record.

scoped-platform-extension.definition: A vendor or platform property without a portable standard equivalent that a named profile scopes explicitly, such as Electron drag regions.
scoped-platform-extension.proof: Scoped admission (E2), emitted CSS (E3) and computed behavior on the exact platform engine (E4) when required; otherwise a scoped diagnostic (E2).

deprecated-or-experimental.definition: Deprecated, experimental, non-standard, abandoned-draft, unimplemented-specification, obsolete-engine-prefix or divergent-legacy-variant entries. A divergent legacy variant is a BCD prefix/alternative name whose documented grammar or values differ from its target. They remain in the denominator with a replacement or equivalent where one exists.
deprecated-or-experimental.proof: A structured diagnostic fixture (E2). Experimental entries also need a CE-11 target fact record (E1) before any promotion. A divergent legacy variant that still ships and may be emitted by the CE-01 transformation (emissionDecision D-BP-07) also needs emitted-CSS proof (E3) restricted to the value subset it shares with its target.

non-css-syntax.definition: An upstream authoring key that is not a CSS property: selector, condition, pseudo-element, axis or multi-property helpers, development helpers and theme keys.
non-css-syntax.proof: An equivalent-capability fixture through canonical PandamStyle mechanisms, or a diagnostic (E2), plus emitted CSS for the equivalent (E3).

incompatible-runtime-requirement.definition: Behavior that requires runtime script binding or unbounded runtime values. It has no static CSS equivalent.
incompatible-runtime-requirement.proof: A negative diagnostic fixture (E2) and a visible limitation record.

procedure: 1. Curated records win in this order: incompatibleRuntime, systemResources, nonCssSyntax, platformExtensions, aliases, deprecated, experimental, nonstandard.
2. Names with an obsolete-engine prefix (-ms-, -o-, -khtml-) are deprecated-or-experimental/obsolete-engine-prefix; their current equivalent is recorded, CE-01 owns the engine incompatibility.
3. Otherwise a BCD css.properties status decides: standard track and neither deprecated nor experimental is a canonical property; deprecated, experimental and non-standard keep that subkind.

4. A name without BCD status that BCD records as a prefix or alternative name of another property is a normalized alias of that property when the target is canonical; otherwise it inherits the target's deprecated or experimental disposition. When the relating BCD statements carry notes, partial implementation or flags, an aliasAudit verdict is required: grammar-divergent makes the name a deprecated-or-experimental/divergent-legacy-variant of the target, behavior-caveat-only keeps the alias with the audit recorded. A behavior-caveat-only verdict on notes that mention syntax or values (derive-registry.mjs GRAMMAR_HINT) needs grammarHintReviewed. A stale or missing verdict fails the build.
5. A remaining -webkit-/-moz- name whose unprefixed base is an inventory entry follows its base in the same way; a vendor-only name is deprecated-or-experimental/nonstandard.

6. Any remaining name is a build error. Every entry must also match exactly one family; the family supplies the capability family, the owner of canonical/platform entries and the profiles that require them.

7. An entry's capability family is its curated requirementCarrier, else its family's. Its owner is curated, else set by disposition subkind (aliases CE-02), else its family's owner; the owner must belong to that capability's coverage Work lots, except CAP-01 and the CE-01/CE-02/CE-11 disposition owners of non-canonical entries.
8. overlayRequirements add the rtl and svg-media overlay profiles to a canonical entry that some application profile already requires and that matches the overlay's names or patterns.

limitations.title: Unbounded runtime CSS values
limitations.statement: StyleX dynamic function styles and Panda runtime values need an inline custom-property or value channel. PandamStyle admits only finite authenticated selections; behavior that truly needs unrestricted runtime values is a product limitation, never approximated by bucketing and labeled equivalent.
limitations.evidence: core-evolution-coverage.md Explicit architecture dispositions; core-evolution-upstreams.md StyleX dynamic values and Panda dynamic selection rows

limitations.title: Runtime style injection
limitations.statement: Runtime stylesheet injection, including development helpers, is excluded. Stylesheets and HMR must work under restrictive CSP; AG-13 owns removal of inherited display surfaces.
limitations.evidence: core-evolution-coverage.md; StyleX 0.19.1 unplugin devMode 'full' injects runtime and HTML in development

limitations.title: Arbitrary consumer selectors, tokens or policy overrides
limitations.statement: Replaced with declared project vocabulary. Upstream arbitrary-selector equivalence is not claimed; unauthorized selectors fail validation in every authoring context.

limitations.title: Runtime DOM and native API behavior
limitations.statement: Opening dialogs, starting a native view transition or driving scroll position is application behavior. The styling contract, attributes and native API dependency are qualified together; CSS alone does not implement them.

limitations.title: Obsolete engines
limitations.statement: Internet Explorer, legacy EdgeHTML, Presto and KHTML are unsupported platforms. Their prefixed entries remain in the registry denominator as obsolete-engine-prefix dispositions; CE-01 records the incompatibility.

limitations.title: Unshipped or partially shipped browser features
limitations.statement: A feature without stable support in a profile target is native-only progressive enhancement or needs an approved equivalent; it never receives a general support label. Required in-profile capabilities without an equivalent block that profile.
limitations.evidence: BCD 8.1.6 statements in registry entries; D-BP-06

limitations.title: Platform-scoped desktop and vendor extensions
limitations.statement: Electron and vendor extensions such as -webkit-app-region are scoped to their exact Chromium/Electron profile and are not portable browser CSS.

limitations.title: Panda responsive variants with compound variants
limitations.statement: Panda 2.2.0 rejects responsive variant values on recipes with compound variants. PandamStyle must define and prove its finite condition-state semantics if the accepted corpus needs the combination; the upstream restriction is disclosed, not inherited silently.

limitations.title: Script-binding CSS properties
limitations.statement: behavior (IE HTML Components) and -moz-binding (XBL) attach script behavior through CSS. They are incompatible runtime requirements with no static equivalent.
